title: September 2019 Class Block 3 Supplementary College Final Exam (Part 1 of 6)
unit: Comprehensive Nursing (Fundamentals, Nursing Theory, Ethics and Law, Infection Prevention, Anatomy and Physiology, Pharmacology Calculations)

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the September 2019 class Block 3 Supplementary College Final Exam paper (Kenya Registered Nursing, sat 6 December 2022, Multiple Choice Questions, Q1 to Q20).

questions.text: The nursing theorist who broke down nursing activities into 14 basic human needs is: -
questions.explanation: Virginia Henderson (A) is correct because her definition of nursing is built on 14 components of basic nursing care (breathing, eating and drinking, elimination, movement and posture, sleep and rest, dressing, body temperature, hygiene, safety, communication, worship, work, recreation and learning), and the nurse helps the individual to meet these needs until he or she can do so independently. Dorothea Orem (B) is incorrect because her Self-Care Deficit theory focuses on the person's ability to perform self-care and when nursing is needed. Hildegard Peplau (C) is incorrect because her theory describes the nurse-patient relationship and its phases (orientation, identification, exploitation, resolution). Florence Nightingale (D) is incorrect because her Environmental theory focuses on manipulating the environment (ventilation, light, cleanliness, quiet, diet) to promote healing.

questions.text: The role the nurse plays when helping a client recognize and cope with stressful psychological problems is: -
questions.explanation: Counsellor (C) is correct because in the counsellor role the nurse helps the client to identify and clarify problems, to recognise and cope with stressful psychological or social problems, to develop improved interpersonal relationships and to promote personal growth. Advocate (A) is incorrect because the advocate protects the client's rights and speaks on the client's behalf. Care giver (B) is incorrect because it covers the delivery of direct physical and psychosocial care and comfort. Manager (D) is incorrect because the manager plans, organises, delegates and coordinates care and resources.

questions.text: A nurse threatens to lock a patient up in the room when the patient refuses to take cooperate. The nurse will be charged with: -
questions.explanation: Assault (A) is correct because assault is an intentional threat, by words or actions, that puts a person in fear of imminent harm or unlawful restraint, even if the threat is not carried out, and here the nurse only threatens to lock up the patient. False imprisonment (B) is incorrect because it requires actual confinement or restraint of the patient without legal authority or consent; it would apply if the nurse had really locked the patient in. Battery (C) is incorrect because it is the actual unconsented touching or physical contact. Intrusion on seclusion (D) is incorrect because it is an invasion of privacy, such as intruding into a person's private affairs or space. Note: if the room had actually been locked, false imprisonment would apply, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: When nurses focus on performing procedures for the well-being of the patient, they conform to the principle of: -
questions.explanation: Beneficence (D) is correct because it is the ethical principle of doing good and acting for the benefit and well-being of the patient, and performing procedures to promote the patient's health fulfils it. Veracity (A) is incorrect because it is the duty to tell the truth. Fidelity (B) is incorrect because it is faithfulness, keeping promises and commitments to the patient. Autonomy (C) is incorrect because it is respect for the patient's right to make his or her own decisions.

questions.text: A positive balance in fluid administration refers to when: -

options.A: An individual void more urine than fluids taken
options.B: The intake is more than the output
options.C: The fluid taken is equal to fluid lost
options.D: An individual does not take any fluids in a day

questions.explanation: The intake is more than the output (B) is correct because a positive fluid balance means that the total fluid taken in (oral, intravenous, tube feeds) is greater than the total fluid lost (urine, stool, vomit, drainage, insensible losses), so fluid is retained, which can cause oedema and weight gain. An individual voids more urine than fluids taken (A) is incorrect because it describes a negative balance. The fluid taken is equal to fluid lost (C) is incorrect because it describes a balanced (equilibrium) state. An individual does not take any fluids in a day (D) is incorrect because it would produce a negative balance, with dehydration.

questions.text: A dirty wound covered with grease should first be cleaned using: -
questions.explanation: Soapy water (C) is correct because grease and dirt must first be removed mechanically, and soap acts as a detergent that emulsifies the grease and lifts the dirt, after which the wound is rinsed with clean water or normal saline and an antiseptic is applied if needed. Bacteranious (bactericidal) solution (A) is incorrect because an antiseptic cannot work well when the wound is covered with grease and dirt. Isopropyl solution (B) is incorrect because alcohol is a skin disinfectant that is painful and tissue-damaging in an open wound, and it does not remove grease well. Glutaraldehyde solution (D) is incorrect because it is a high-level disinfectant for instruments and is toxic to tissues, so it is never used on a wound.

questions.text: Baby X is to get 150ml of Normal Saline for over 4 hours using a soluset. Calculate flow rate.
questions.explanation: 38gtt/min (A) is correct because a soluset (burette set) delivers 60 drops per ml, and the flow rate is (volume in ml x drop factor) divided by (time in minutes): (150 x 60) / (4 x 60) = 9000 / 240 = 37.5, which is rounded to 38 drops per minute. 20gtt/min (B), 12gtt/min (C) and 10gtt/min (D) are incorrect because they result from using the wrong drop factor (for example 15 or 20 drops per ml, as in a standard adult giving set) or from a calculation error.

questions.text: A system related drug error during drug administration is: -
questions.explanation: Poor work flow (D) is correct because system-related errors arise from the way the organisation is set up (poor work flow and processes, staffing, interruptions, inadequate policies, environment), rather than from the individual. Poor calculation (A) is incorrect because it is a human (individual) error in knowledge or skill. Illegible handwriting (B) is incorrect because it is a human error in prescribing, although it can be reduced by a system change. Look alike sound alike drugs (C) is incorrect as the best answer because it is a product-related (drug labelling and packaging) cause. Note: look-alike drugs and illegible handwriting can also be classed as system factors, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: An example of a low flow oxygen delivery system is: -
questions.explanation: Partial rebreather mask (B) is correct because low-flow systems supply oxygen at a flow lower than the patient's inspiratory demand, so the patient also breathes in room air and the delivered concentration varies (nasal cannula, simple face mask, partial rebreather and non-rebreather masks; the partial rebreather gives about 60 to 90% at 6 to 10 L/min). Venturi (A) is incorrect because it is a high-flow (fixed performance) system that gives a precise oxygen concentration. Bag valve mask (C) is incorrect because it is a manual resuscitation device for assisted ventilation. Oxygen tent (D) is incorrect as the best answer because it is a bulky enclosure used mainly for children, with a variable and low concentration. Note: an oxygen tent is also classed as low flow by some texts, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: During limb observation the nurse instructs the patient to close their eyes when assessing: -
questions.explanation: Paresthesia (C) is correct because sensation (tingling, numbness, response to light touch or pinprick) is tested with the patient's eyes closed, so that the patient cannot see where the nurse is touching and the answer is based on feeling alone. Pain (A) is incorrect because the patient reports pain verbally and does not need to close the eyes. Peripheral pulses (B) is incorrect because they are assessed by palpation, and the patient can have the eyes open. Paralysis (D) is incorrect because movement and muscle power are tested by asking the patient to move the limb, which is observed with the eyes open.

questions.text: Patient X has neutropenia. The appropriate isolation type is: -
questions.explanation: Protective (A) is correct because a neutropenic patient has a very low neutrophil count and a weak defence against infection, so protective (reverse) isolation is used, in which the patient is placed in a single room and staff and visitors perform hand hygiene and wear a mask and gown as needed, to keep microorganisms away from the patient. Airborne (B) is incorrect because it is used for diseases spread by small particles, such as TB, measles and chickenpox. Contact (C) is incorrect because it is used for diseases spread by touch, such as MRSA and scabies. Droplet (D) is incorrect because it is used for diseases spread by large droplets, such as meningococcal meningitis, mumps and whooping cough.

questions.text: The correct sequence of physical examination on the abdomen is: -
questions.explanation: Inspection, Auscultation, Percussion, Palpation (D) is correct because in the abdomen auscultation is done before percussion and palpation, so that these do not change the bowel activity and the bowel sounds, and palpation comes last, as it is the most likely to cause discomfort or change the findings. Palpation, Percussion, Auscultation, Inspection (A) is incorrect because it reverses the order. Inspection, Palpation, Percussion, Auscultation (B) is incorrect because it is the sequence for the other body systems, and it would alter the bowel sounds. Inspection, Auscultation, Palpation, Percussion (C) is incorrect because percussion comes before palpation in the abdomen.

questions.text: A nurse is using SBAR to communicate to the doctor. The following statements indicate “A”: -

options.A: The patient needs to be evaluated immediately
options.C: The patient is complaining of difficulty in breathing

questions.explanation: The patient oxygen level is 75% (D) is correct because in SBAR the 'A' stands for Assessment, in which the nurse gives the objective findings (vital signs, oxygen saturation) and her interpretation of the problem. The patient needs to be evaluated immediately (A) is incorrect because it is the Recommendation (R). The patient was admitted yesterday (B) is incorrect because it is the Background (B). The patient is complaining of difficulty in breathing (C) is incorrect because it states the Situation (S), the reason for the call.

questions.text: The following is true about nursing documentation: -

options.A: You can document assessment conducted by another nurse
options.B: Document at the end of the shift
options.C: The nurse can document in advance before performing the procedure
options.D: All documents should have the signature of the nurse documenting

questions.explanation: All documents should have the signature of the nurse documenting (D) is correct because every entry must be signed (with name, designation and date and time) so that it is accountable, authentic and legally valid. You can document assessment conducted by another nurse (A) is incorrect because a nurse documents only what she has personally done or observed. Document at the end of the shift (B) is incorrect because entries should be made promptly, at the time of or soon after care, to be accurate. The nurse can document in advance before performing the procedure (C) is incorrect because documenting care before it is given is falsification of records.

questions.text: The first step in donning PPE with a full body suit is: -

options.B: Don the first pair of gloves

questions.explanation: Perform hand hygiene (D) is correct because hand hygiene is always the first step before putting on PPE (and is repeated after removing it), so that the equipment is not contaminated by the hands. Wear the hair net (A), Don the first pair of gloves (B) and Put on the goggles (C) are incorrect because they are later steps in the sequence, which in general is: hand hygiene, gown or body suit, mask or respirator, eye protection (goggles or face shield) and gloves last.

questions.text: Droplet transmission based isolation precautions is indicated in: -
questions.explanation: Mumps, Meningococcal meningitis (C) is correct because both are spread by large respiratory droplets, so droplet precautions (a single room, a surgical mask within about 1 metre of the patient) are used. Pulmonary Tuberculosis, Diphtheria (A) is incorrect because pulmonary TB needs airborne precautions, even though diphtheria (respiratory) is a droplet disease. Measles, Whooping cough (B) is incorrect because measles needs airborne precautions, even though whooping cough is a droplet disease. Chicken pox, Miliary tuberculosis (D) is incorrect because chickenpox needs airborne (and contact) precautions, and miliary TB is not infectious unless there is also pulmonary disease.

questions.text: An example of a positive feedback mechanism is: -
questions.explanation: Uterine contractions during labor (B) is correct because in a positive feedback mechanism the response amplifies the original stimulus: pressure of the baby's head on the cervix stimulates oxytocin release, which makes the uterus contract more strongly, which pushes the head harder on the cervix, until the baby is delivered. Others examples are blood clotting and lactation. Regulation of core body temperature (A), Blood pressure regulation (C) and Blood glucose maintenance (D) are incorrect because they are negative feedback mechanisms, which reverse the change and keep the variable near its set point (homeostasis).

questions.text: The functions of simple squamous epithelial cells include: -
questions.explanation: Diffusion, lubrication (A) is correct because simple squamous epithelium is a single thin layer of flat cells, which allows diffusion, osmosis and filtration (alveoli, capillary walls, Bowman's capsule) and, as mesothelium of the serous membranes, secretes a lubricating fluid that reduces friction. Absorption, protection (B) is incorrect because absorption is the function of simple columnar epithelium (intestine) and protection is the function of stratified squamous epithelium (skin). Secretion, transportation (C) is incorrect because secretion is done by glandular and columnar epithelium and transport by ciliated columnar epithelium. Distention, absorption (D) is incorrect because distension is a function of transitional epithelium (bladder). Note: the handwritten mark on the scanned paper is on option B, but simple squamous epithelium is not an absorptive or protective tissue, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Hair cells responsible for balance are located in the: -
questions.explanation: Utricle (A) is correct because the utricle (and saccule) of the vestibule contains the maculae, which are patches of hair cells covered by otoliths that detect the position of the head (static equilibrium) and linear acceleration. Semicircular canal (B) is incorrect as the best answer because the hair cells in the ampullae (cristae) detect rotation of the head (dynamic equilibrium), although they also help with balance. Spiral organ (C) is incorrect because the organ of Corti in the cochlea contains hair cells for hearing. Oval window (D) is incorrect because it is a membrane-covered opening between the middle ear and the inner ear and has no hair cells. Note: hair cells in the semicircular canals also contribute to balance, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Rods are: -

options.A: Responsible for vision at low light levels
options.C: Exclusively populated at the central fovea

questions.explanation: Responsible for vision at low light levels (A) is correct because rods contain the pigment rhodopsin, which is very sensitive to dim light, so they give night (scotopic) vision in black, white and grey, and are found mostly in the periphery of the retina. Active at high light levels (B) is incorrect because it describes cones. Exclusively populated at the central fovea (C) is incorrect because the fovea contains only cones, and there are no rods in it. Responsible for visualizing colors (D) is incorrect because colour vision is a function of the cones.
